junction.name: 4th Avenue South & South Spokane Street, Seattle

claims.text: 4th Avenue South & South Spokane Street had 19 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
These counts are 4th Avenue South & South Spokane Street's own: the city's record places 139 of the 180 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.3 million a year (injury crashes only: deaths are not valued in this figure).
81% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck motor vehicle, front end at angle” crashes, against 43% at the city's worst crash locations.
39% of crashes here were recorded as “angles” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
39% of crashes here were recorded as “entering at angle” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.6 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $195,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $125,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 4th Avenue South, South Spokane Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
